clue.text: Call to imprison a pair of bishops displaying cross

indicators.note: the call word holds the other pieces inside it as a prisoner

parts.note: to call out is to cry
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two of them give BB

explanation.surface: A churchy scene where locking up two bishops makes someone look angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross means irritable or bad-tempered, a plain synonym for crabby.

clue.text: Company keeps packaging minute luxuries

indicators.note: the company and keep words wrap around the minute letter

parts.note: a keep is the stronghold of a castle, so keeps are forts

explanation.surface: A business holds back on wrapping tiny luxury goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps' looks like a verb but is the plural noun for castle strongholds.
explanation.definitionFit: Comforts are things that make life pleasant, such as creature comforts, i.e. luxuries.

clue.text: Acted in play about Juliet — I have part of speech to modify

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the Juliet letter
letters in play are moving freely, so they are rearranged

parts.note: J is Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: An actor playing Juliet speaks of having a part to adapt.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an actor rehearsing Romeo and Juliet; the dash hides that 'I have' is simply contracted and tacked on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective is the word class used to describe or qualify a noun.

clue.text: Jeer when boozer goes to stand

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub, a bar
a rack is a stand for holding things

explanation.surface: Heckling breaks out when a drinker gets up.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is the British word for heckling or shouting abuse at a performer or player.

clue.text: Small economic unit that's broken up now

definitions.text: Small economic unit that's broken up now

parts.words: Small economic unit that's broken up now
parts.note: the old single-word coin sum is nowadays written as two words, the number and the plural of penny, so it has been split apart

explanation.walkthrough: In pre-decimal Britain the sum was one word (said 'tuppence'); since decimalisation it is usually written TWO PENCE, so the unit is literally broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sum of British money, a modest economic unit once written as one word and now as two.

clue.text: Recurring break seen after a fall?

definitions.text: Recurring break seen after a fall?

parts.words: Recurring break seen after a fall?
parts.note: the annual holiday that comes round each year, of the kind that is seen after a fall of snow

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' suggests an accident causing a broken bone; it is a snowfall, and the break is the yearly holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowy festive season, dreamed of in the Bing Crosby song, follows a fall of snow.

clue.text: Page to blame for yielding

parts.note: liable means responsible, to blame

explanation.surface: A servant boy is accused of giving way.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliable means flexible or easily bent, readily giving way under pressure.

clue.text: Listeners should support new approaches

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits below the other one

parts.note: ears are what we listen with

explanation.surface: Audiences ought to back fresh ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Nears is a verb meaning comes closer to, so approaches.

clue.text: Covers of Elvis, Voice singer's top compositions

indicators.note: the covers of a word are its outside letters

parts.note: to voice is to say

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A TV talent contestant covers Elvis numbers, writes the singer at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The Voice is a TV singing contest, a misleading nod to cover versions.
explanation.definitionFit: Essays are short written compositions, as set at school.

clue.text: I bid on projects for work, seeing this?

definitions.text: I bid on projects for work, seeing this?

indicators.note: to work something is to shape it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A contractor bids for projects after reading what the role involves.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: someone reads this before bidding for work.
explanation.definitionFit: A job description sets out a role's duties, the document an applicant reads before seeking the work.

clue.text: Outstanding kind of key officer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a musical key such as C ...
third meaning: an army rank above captain

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for importance, a musical mode, and a military rank between captain and lieutenant colonel.

clue.text: Masters exam's cracked by one with spirit

indicators.note: the exam word is broken open and the other pieces sit in the gap

parts.note: orals are spoken examinations; read as plural exams
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A student's master's exam is disrupted by someone who has been drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Masters as in original works of art or master recordings, from which copies are made.

clue.text: It contains fruit or vegetable

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether something holds fruit or vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot of fruit trees, so it holds fruit growing on them.

clue.text: Electronic guitar — possessing this is my mission

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: the word my holds the guitar inside it as a possession

parts.note: a bass is a bass guitar

explanation.surface: A musician declares that owning an electric guitar is their purpose in life.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic mission is the staff or building of an ambassador abroad, the same as an embassy.

clue.text: With King attending, smash hit Chess and Evita close

indicators.note: smash means the letters are broken and reassembled; it also plays on smash hit

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A royal attends a run of hit musicals, Chess and Evita.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smash hit' reads as one phrase about the shows, but 'smash' alone is the anagram signal working on HIT, CHESS, EVITA and K.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes people who are very intimate or in league, so it means close as friends.

clue.text: Decide whether to break up railway — or upgrade?

parts.note: to elect is to choose or decide

indicators.note: the whether word breaks the railway letters apart

parts.note: if means whether

explanation.surface: Planners must choose between closing a railway line and modernising it.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrifying a railway line modernises it from steam or diesel, an improvement.

clue.text: Idiots dropping ecstasy annoyed judge

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: the annoyed word drops a letter

parts.note: sore means annoyed or aggrieved
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Fools giving up drugs irritate a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping ecstasy' sounds like taking the drug; here it takes E out of SORE.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor evaluates or judges things, such as an insurance claim or exam work.

clue.text: The old upper town residents?

parts.note: senior means higher in rank, upper
citizens are the inhabitants of a town or city

explanation.surface: A question about whether older people are the posh, uphill residents of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior citizens is a polite name for elderly people, the old as a group.

clue.text: Introduce this person's idea to be on time

parts.note: this person is I, the setter, and this person's here means I am, contracted to I'm
a plan is an idea

explanation.surface: Someone claims their idea will be delivered punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: To implant is to put something in, to introduce it into a body or mind.

clue.text: Laziness makes the writer retain eccentric style

parts.note: the writer is the setter, who refers to themselves as I

indicators.note: letters given an eccentric style are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: An author's idleness leads them to cling to an odd way of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a lack of energy or will to act, sluggishness.

clue.text: Awkward, this being left in Calais

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the French word for left, as used in Calais, a French port

explanation.walkthrough: English borrowed the French word for left-handed to mean socially clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means tactless or socially inept, and in French it simply means the opposite of right.

clue.text: Something going to the head local cop, opponent claims

indicators.note: the phrase claims the answer, holding it within its letters across the words

explanation.surface: A rival says a local police officer is an intoxicating influence.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across local, cop and opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sweet alcoholic drink, and drink is something that goes to your head.

clue.text: Jacket worn by head of the class

indicators.note: the jacket is worn by the head letter, wrapping around it

parts.note: a case or jacket is an outer covering, as for a book

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The school's head boy or girl wears a blazer.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, as in the traditional Indian system.

clue.text: Start to think about limiting high temperature in place of surgery

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing on either side, so the outer letters hold the warmth word
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: re means about, concerning
heat is high temperature

explanation.surface: A doctor considers whether to keep a fever down before the operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The operating theatre is the room where surgery is done, so 'place of surgery' is a hospital sense, not a GP's consulting room.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating theatre is the room in a hospital where surgeons operate.

clue.text: Item from flamenco star I caught here?

definitions.text: Item from flamenco star I caught here?

indicators.note: the answer is an item taken from inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A tourist wonders whether a souvenir from a flamenco dancer was picked up in this country.
explanation.walkthrough: The country runs across flamenco, star, I and caught; the whole clue also asks where you might have caught a flamenco star's keepsake.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a Central American country, a place where a holidaymaker might pick up such an item.

clue.text: It's dry gin for use essentially all in small units

indicators.note: the essence of each of all these words is its centre letter

explanation.surface: A recipe note says dry gin is meant to be used in small measures.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the middle letter of each of five words: ITS, DRY, GIN, FOR, USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trios are groups of three, so small units of people or musicians.

clue.text: Energy finding an outlet in sport

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
venting is letting something out through an outlet

explanation.surface: Pent-up energy is released through a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is the equestrian competition combining dressage, cross-country and showjumping.

clue.text: Wife's appearance in film will be brief

indicators.note: the wife letter makes an appearance inside the film word

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, as of dust
W is the abbreviation for wife, read here as wife has

explanation.surface: A spouse's cameo in a movie will be short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' reads as an adjective meaning short; it is the noun, a barrister's informal name.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is informal slang for a lawyer, from the legal brief a barrister is given.
